implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines replaces the blocking monitor with suspension: the documentation presents Channel as the non-blocking counterpart of BlockingQueue whose send/receive suspend instead of blocking, a rendezvous channel makes send wait for a receiver (the same handoff as a guarded take), and Mutex.withLock plus a re-checked predicate covers guards that are not queue-shaped. Because a suspended coroutine holds no thread, this is the default realization for Kotlin services; the JVM intrinsic monitor remains for thread-affine code that cannot adopt coroutines, and calling blocking JDK primitives inside a coroutine steals a dispatcher thread instead of suspending.
pitfalls: Prompt cancellation can drop a value that was already taken from a channel: pass an onUndeliveredElement handler when the payload owns a resource.
Blocking calls (Thread.sleep, JDK blocking queues) inside a coroutine stall the dispatcher instead of suspending, so the notifier cannot run.
A channel used as a one-to-many broadcast needs an explicit close; without it every for-loop over the channel stays suspended forever.

variants.name: JVM intrinsic monitor (synchronized + Object.wait/notifyAll)
variants.implementation_notes: On the JVM, Kotlin inherits java.lang.Object monitors unchanged: synchronized(lock) { while (!predicate()) (lock as java.lang.Object).wait() } with notifyAll from the mutating side is the classic guarded suspension, and Kotlin's stdlib adds lock helpers but no condition-variable abstraction, so the predicate loop and the signalling contract stay hand-written. Use it in libraries that must not depend on kotlinx.coroutines or when the guarded state is thread-affine behind an external lock; note that a parked wait() cannot be cancelled by coroutine cancellation.
pitfalls: A blocked Object.wait() ignores coroutine cancellation, so a cancellable API must expose a timeout or move to suspension.
Calling synchronized from a coroutine on Dispatchers.Default occupies a dispatcher thread for the whole wait, shrinking the pool.
